title: Act on the first play test

needs: Fix what blocked or confused the first outside tester, who played 0.1.38 for 52 minutes on a 13-inch laptop, cleared stages 1 to 3 and stopped at stage 4.
Keep the tester's raw material private: notes here are paraphrased, with no name, recording or screenshot from the session.
context: Play test of 2026-11-24, one tester who plays Factorio a lot and compares with it; the raw transcript and four screenshots are kept outside the repository.
Liked: the music, recipes that read clearly once the core's sheet is found, the Ligase's input swap once discovered, the right click to dismantle.
Blocking: at stage 4 two identical assembler and encapsulator setups behaved differently, one consuming its inputs and the other not; the tester stopped there.
Sound: music loud at launch with no master volume; the game and the music pause when the window loses focus, which the tester would like as an option.
Small screen: the core's sheet with its recipes runs behind the bottom dock on a 13-inch screen and cannot be scrolled.
Hidden information: what MK2, MK3 and the large harvester add is unclear; the options a machine offers when clicked (rank, swap, empty) were found late; Empty disappears from the sheet once used.
Controls: no H and V flip keys (the swap exists only in the machine's sheet), the eyedropper (Q) went unnoticed, a click in rotate mode turns the piece unexpectedly.

Lines: drawing and dismantling sometimes extend a line and sometimes start a perpendicular one; some turns are taken and others refused; a line passing beside a harvester links to it; a line drawn from a harvester did not start where expected; a bridge cannot be dismantled without breaking the line before it; the direction of a belt reads poorly.
Reading the board: empty Ligase inputs drawn in red look like errors.

Room and pace: the ground round the core fills fast; each stage's recipes call for new lines, so the tester tore everything down at each stage; waiting for counts such as 50 felt long; stage 4 felt like stage 3 again.
Purpose: the splitter, the fights and the mutations seemed optional, since no fight was needed to progress.
Statistics: one production stopped while another went on, with nothing saying why.
Suggestion: let a harvester's output pass under a line like a bridge.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The stage 4 assembler and encapsulator case is reproduced from the tester's description, its cause fixed or explained in the game, and covered by a test.
AC2: Sound has a master volume, a quieter first start, and an option to keep playing when the window is hidden.
AC3: The core's sheet, the trays and the machine sheets stay readable and scrollable on a 1280 by 720 screen and on phones.
AC4: Ranks, large harvesters and machine options say what they give where the player looks, and Empty stays available after use.
AC5: H and V flip what can be flipped, the eyedropper and other keys are shown where they act, and rotate mode no longer turns a piece by surprise.
AC6: Drawing and dismantling lines follow one rule the player can predict, documented in the help, with tests for each case the tester met.
AC7: Empty inputs no longer read as errors, and a belt's direction reads at a glance.
AC8: Room and progression are reviewed: space round the core, lines that carry over between stages, waits and stage variety, and a reason to fight, each with a decision recorded.

backlog_items.title: Reproduce and fix the stage 4 assembler and encapsulator case
problem: Two setups the tester saw as identical gave different results: one assembled and encapsulated, the other kept its inputs; the tester could not tell why and stopped.
scope_in: Rebuild the stage 4 recipes the tester faced (two genes joined then encapsulated) in a test, try each side and order of entry, find what differs.
Fix a fault, or show in the machine's sheet why it waits (wrong half, wrong side, wrong box).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A test reproduces the case.
AC2: The machine either works or says in its sheet what it waits for.

backlog_items.title: Give sound a master volume and a choice to play on in the background
problem: Music is loud at first launch and only music and effects have volumes; the game and the music stop when the window is hidden.
scope_in: A master volume over music and effects, kept between visits.
A lower default music level at first launch.
A setting to keep the game and the music running when the window is hidden.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The audio settings have a master volume that scales music and effects.
AC2: The background setting keeps the simulation and the music running while hidden.

backlog_items.title: Fit the core's sheet and the panels on small screens
problem: On a 13-inch screen the core's sheet runs behind the bottom dock and cannot be scrolled.
scope_in: Sheets and trays bounded by the space above the dock, scrolling inside.
Browser tests at 1280 by 720 and at phone sizes.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: At 1280 by 720 every row of the core's sheet can be reached.
AC2: No sheet overlaps the dock.

backlog_items.title: Say what ranks, large harvesters and machine options give
problem: The gains of MK2, MK3 and the large harvester are unclear, the options on a click are found late, and Empty vanishes after use.
scope_in: The help of a building follows the rank picked, with its numbers.
A first selection of a machine points at its options.
Empty stays in the sheet while the machine can hold items, with a key.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Each rank button shows what it changes in numbers.
AC2: Empty stays offered after use.

backlog_items.title: Add flip keys and make the keys and rotate mode predictable
problem: The swap of a Ligase, an encapsulator or a joiner exists only in its sheet; the eyedropper went unnoticed; a click in rotate mode turns a piece by surprise.
scope_in: H and V flip the piece in hand or under the pointer where it has sides to swap.
Keys shown in the tooltips of the dock and the sheets.
Rotate mode: a click selects, the rotate key turns.
scope_out: Mirroring of shapes that have no side to swap.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: H and V swap the sides of every machine that has a swap button.
AC2: The eyedropper key is shown in the dock's tooltips.
AC3: A test covers a click in rotate mode.

backlog_items.title: Make drawing and dismantling lines follow one rule
problem: A drag sometimes extends a line and sometimes starts a perpendicular one; turns are sometimes refused; lines link to a harvester they pass; a bridge cannot be removed alone; a belt's direction reads poorly.
scope_in: One written rule for extend, turn and branch, shown in the help.
A line links to a harvester only when it starts or ends on it.
Dismantling a bridge leaves the belt under it.
A clearer arrow on belts.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Tests cover extend, turn, branch, passing beside a harvester and dismantling a bridge.
AC2: The help describes the rule.

backlog_items.title: Stop empty inputs from reading as errors
problem: Empty Ligase inputs are drawn with red rings, which reads as a fault.
scope_in: A neutral mark for an empty input; red kept for a real fault.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: An empty Ligase input is drawn without red in 2D and 3D.

backlog_items.title: Review room, carry-over between stages, waits and the reason to fight
problem: The ground round the core fills fast, each stage made the tester tear down the last one, waits felt long, stage 4 felt like stage 3, and fights seemed optional; one production stopped in the statistics with no reason given.
scope_in: A design note with a decision on each point: room round the core, recipes that reuse earlier lines, counts and waits, variety between stages 3 and 4, what makes fights needed.
The statistics say why a production stopped.
The harvester-as-bridge suggestion answered.
scope_out: Implementing every idea in this item: each decision taken becomes its own item.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A design note records a decision for each point.
AC2: The statistics name the cause of a stopped production.

orchestration_task.title: Orchestrate the fixes from the first play test
plan: Start after the modularization request req_002 is delivered, unless the operator moves a fix ahead.
First the blocking case (assembler and encapsulator), then sound and small screens, then controls and lines, then readability, then the design review.
Each fix: reproduce, fix, test, commit; push once CI is green; release when the operator asks, then ask the tester to replay.
